Subject: Kickoff: Embeddings & Rerank migration — Liberty Financial

Sarah — great to meet last week. Per our call, pushing a short kickoff note to align on scope, timeline, and a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get your search cutover de-risked.

Ask: can you confirm availability for a 60-min kickoff next Tue (7/7) morning PT?

High-level scope (what Redwood will help with):
- Index backfill architecture (snapshot + incremental / streaming ingestion)
- Vector DB selection and migration plan (tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs retention)
- Rerank evaluation: sample set, acceptance criteria, smoke tests
- Canary/cutover playbook and rollback triggers

Initial data asks (to prep the kickoff):
1) Current vector count & average dimension size
2) Typical QPS and peak QPS window (P50/P95 latency targets)
3) A short list of 10 representative queries + expected top-3 results (for rerank priming)

I've attached a one-pager outline we can iterate on (migration_plan_outline.pdf). Mateo and Monica will lead the implementation coordination from Redwood. Ben will surface DB tradeoffs.

Karthik / Mateo / Monica — thanks for the note. Tue 7/7 10am PT works for us. Invited Derek and I will be there.

Quick data points to unblock planning:
- We currently store ~18,200,000 vectors (768d), exported from ShardVector (hosted).
- Average payload per vector (metadata) is ~460 bytes; total index size ~13.2GB compressed.
- Typical QPS: 120 steady, peaks up to 950 during statement cycles (monthly). Target end-to-end P95 <= 120ms for interactive UI.

Constraints / compliance notes: we cannot export raw PII fields. We can provide a sanitized CSV with vector ids, embedding rows, and hashed doc ids — attached (liberty_export_summary.csv).

We'll prepare the 10 sample queries you requested and a short acceptance criteria doc ahead of the kickoff.

Cheers,

Sarah — thanks for the numbers and for sanitizing the export. That gives us a concrete basis for sizing.

Short internal plan I want to run by you at kickoff (we'll cover more detail in the call):
Phase A — Discovery (this week)
- Confirm sample queries / golden answers
- Baseline current retrieval + rerank quality (we'll compute MRR/Recall on provided set)
- Evaluate latency budget with a small live load test (dev cluster)

Phase B — Pilot/Canary (2 weeks)
- Run an incremental backfill to a candidate vectorstore (option A: Milvus self-hosted; option B: managed Pinecone)
- Rerank model should be pinned to the version we validated in discovery; we'll run shadow traffic and compare results
- Define SLOs and rollback thresholds (quality and latency)

Phase C — Cutover & Backfill (1–3 weeks depending on index size)
- Two-stage backfill: snapshot bulk upload (fast path) + continuous incremental until cutover point
- Dual-read period (both stores serving, Redwood picks winner based on policy)

Ben — can you capture DB options + expected engineering effort and list of infra prerequisites? Monica — I'll leave MAP ownership to you (delivery dates, CS touchpoints).

I'll bring a high-level runbook to the kickoff.

—Mateo
Senior Customer Solutions Manager — Redwood Inference

Quick DB tradeoffs and a suggested checklist from infra/engineering: (notes, not final)
- Option 1: Milvus (self-hosted)
  - Pros: lower unit cost for large index, flexible control over retention and sharding
  - Cons: ops burden; infra network egress constraints may be a blocker for Liberty's security team
- Option 2: Pinecone (managed)
  - Pros: simple onboarding, built-in autoscaling and fine-grained RBAC
  - Cons: higher per-query cost at 1M+ QPS-months; potential vendor lock-in
- Option 3: Redwood-managed store (hybrid)
  - Pros: Redwood handles operational runbook; tight integration with our caching and KV strategies
  - Cons: requires a short contract addendum for dedicated capacity

Implementation checklist (engineering estimates):
- Access: Get sanitized export + S3 write creds (for bulk upload) — 1 day
- Bulk uploader: parallelized shards, resume on failure — 3 days dev + 1 day smoke
- Incremental streamer: CDC connector (our side) — 4 days dev + 2 days testing
- Canary harness: traffic splitter + shadow runner — 3 days dev
- Acceptance harness: batch rerank eval and quick MRR pipeline — 2 days dev

I'll attach a short doc summarizing vendor comparison (vector-db-options.md). Also depends on whether Liberty allows managed infra or requires VPC-only.

Ben
Staff Engineer, Infra — Redwood Inference

Attachments: vector-db-options.md (text/markdown)

Sarah / Derek — nice to meet you on the calendar. Follow-up with our proposed MAP and concrete asks so we can start scheduling sprints: 

Mutual Action Plan (top-level)
- Week 0 (Discovery): share 10 sample queries + golden answers (Liberty) — due 7/6
- Week 1 (Pilot setup): Redwood bootstraps pilot vectorstore; run bulk snapshot test — target 7/9–7/13
- Week 2 (Canary): run shadow rerank on 10k queries, compute MRR/regression — target 7/14–7/20
- Week 3 (Cutover prep): finalize cutover window, run full backfill dry-run — target 7/21–7/25
- Week 4 (Cutover): execute cutover and monitor, rollback window 48 hours — target 7/28–8/1

Deliverables we need from Liberty by 7/6: sanitized export (received), sample queries (pending), security contact for VPC/egress policy, and confirmation of P95 latency target (120ms).

Acceptance checks for rerank (baseline)
- MRR on sample set must be >= current MRR - 2% (regression tolerance)
- No systemic drop in P50 latency; P95 must be within target else fail canary
- No more than 0.5% unserved queries during backfill window

I've attached an evaluation template for rerank (rerank-eval-spec.xlsx). Mateo — I'll sync with you on scheduling the MAP milestones and open a shared drive folder (link in calendar invite).

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Monica / team — thanks, the MAP looks good. Attached is a short file with 12 sample queries + expected top-3 (we added a couple of edge cases) and a short acceptance doc (internal link): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1x2Liberty-acceptance.

Two quick notes:
- We can tolerate up to 3% regression in recall for low-frequency queries, but core business queries (account lookup / balance lookup) must be within 0.5% of current precision.
- Security will require that any managed store is behind a VPC and that egress to 3rd parties is documented. We prefer Redwood-managed in-VPC or self-hosted Milvus inside our cloud tenancy.

See you on Tue 7/7 10am PT for kickoff.
